Both survive because the types package binds

functions/ is the only package that imports from
Everything else imports the specific module it
needs. That is the layering rule the code actually
obeys: the stdlib sits on top of the whole library,
and nothing sits on top of the stdlib.
a module-scope import, taken at load time — the arrow points the way the dependency runs.
reached only under TYPE_CHECKING, or from inside a function body. No load-time dependency.
a module-scope cycle between two packages.
The two group boxes — the wire modules, the value-level modules — are top-level .py files
rather than packages, collected so the graph stays about packages; their arrows are the union of
the group's real imports. Everything here came from the AST of every file under src/pyvider/cty,
not from the docstrings, counting TYPE_CHECKING and function-local imports separately.
